group.passage: Every year, the frozen sea around the North Pole grows and shrinks. The ice spreads across the Arctic Ocean through the long, dark winter and usually reaches its largest area in March. It then melts through the summer and is at its smallest in September. Since 1979, satellites have tracked this yearly rhythm by measuring every area of ocean where at least 15 percent of the surface is covered by ice. The chart compares the average ice cover in these two months over more than four decades. Winter ice has changed fairly little, but the summer figures tell a different story. Since 1979, September ice has been shrinking by about 12 percent per decade, roughly five times faster than the ice in March. The most dramatic year was 2012. In early August, a powerful storm swept across the Arctic and broke a huge piece off the main body of ice. The loose ice melted quickly, and on September 16 the ice covered just 3.41 million square kilometers, the lowest single-day figure in the satellite record. Scientists pointed out that the storm itself was not unusual; what had changed was the ice. In the mid-1980s, up to a third of the winter ice had been thick ice that survived several summers, but by 2020 such old ice made up only about 5 percent. Losing summer ice matters far beyond the Arctic. Bright ice reflects up to 80 percent of the sunlight that reaches it, while dark open water absorbs much more. As more water is exposed, the ocean warms and melts still more ice. This loop is one reason the Arctic is warming faster than the rest of the planet. Animals such as polar bears, walruses and seals, which depend on the ice, are also losing their habitat. The trend is expected to continue. Climate scientists expect the Arctic Ocean to be practically free of ice in September at least once before 2050, with less than 1 million square kilometers left. Records of the distant past suggest that the ice has not retreated this fast in at least 1,500 years.

translation_zh.text:
每一年，北極周圍的冰凍海洋都會擴大又縮小。在漫長黑暗的冬季，海冰向整個北冰洋擴展，通常在 3 月達到最大面積；接著在夏天融化，到 9 月時最小。從 1979 年起，衛星就一直追蹤這個每年的節奏，測量每一片至少有 15% 表面被冰覆蓋的海域。

圖表比較了四十多年來這兩個月份的平均海冰面積。冬季的冰變化不大，夏季的數字卻是另一回事。從 1979 年以來，9 月的海冰每十年縮小約 12%，大約是 3 月海冰縮小速度的五倍。

變化最劇烈的一年是 2012 年。8 月初，一場強烈的風暴席捲北極，從主要的冰體上折斷了一大塊。鬆散的冰很快融化，到了 9 月 16 日，海冰只覆蓋 341 萬平方公里，是衛星紀錄中最低的單日數值。科學家指出，那場風暴本身並不特別；改變的是冰。在 1980 年代中期，冬季海冰中多達三分之一是撐過好幾個夏天的厚冰，但到了 2020 年，這種老冰只占大約 5%。

夏季海冰的消失，影響遠遠超出北極。明亮的冰能反射照到它的陽光的八成，而深色的開闊海水吸收的要多得多。露出的海水越多，海洋就越暖，又融化更多冰。這個循環是北極暖化得比地球其他地方快的原因之一。北極熊、海象和海豹等依賴海冰的動物，也正在失去棲地。

這個趨勢預料還會持續。氣候科學家預估，在 2050 年以前，北冰洋至少會有一年的 9 月幾乎沒有冰，剩下不到 100 萬平方公里。關於遙遠過去的紀錄顯示，至少 1,500 年來，海冰從未退縮得這麼快。

【圖 1】北極海冰範圍，1979–2024（百萬平方公里，每個點是該月平均）：9 月（每年最小）1979 年 7.1、1985 年 6.7、1990 年 6.1、1995 年 6.1、2000 年 6.2、2005 年 5.5、2007 年 4.3、2010 年 4.9、2012 年 3.6、2015 年 4.6、2020 年 4、2024 年 4.4；3 月（每年最大）依序為 16.3、15.9、15.9、15.3、15.2、14.7、14.5、15.1、15.2、14.4、14.7、14.9。

open_tasks.prompt: Using the chart, describe in one or two English sentences how the September and March lines differ, and give one reason from the passage why the difference matters.
reference_answers: The September line drops much more steeply than the March line, which only falls slowly; this matters because less summer ice means more dark water that absorbs sunlight and melts even more ice.
Summer ice has shrunk far more than winter ice, from about 7.1 to 4.4 million square kilometers, so animals like polar bears are losing their habitat.
